PROTOCOLS

From this week’s stories, three skills to try.

MAKE AI WRITE LIKE YOU

From Mike Taylor https://every.?ev_audience=free’s “How I Finally Got AI to Write Like Me” https://every.?ev_audience=free

Mike has been trying to get AI to write like him since 2020. What finally worked was testing drafts against his published posts, not describing his style. He now goes from an opinion to a finished piece in about an hour instead of a day. Here’s how to build your own version:

 * Strip your best work down to the substance. Gather 12–25 recent pieces in one format and set a few aside for a final test. Have AI turn each piece into a plain brief with the thesis, facts, and quotes. The steps https://every.?ev_audience=free
 * Let a judge pick between two drafts. Give an AI judge the original and two drafts from the same brief. Ask which sounds more like the original, then swap the drafts and ask again to account for order bias. The judge https://every.?ev_audience=free
 * Optimize the skill as you go. Test each change with the model you’ll use to draft. Keep the changes that improve the skill’s score, then test the finished skill on the pieces you set aside. The skill https://every.?ev_audience=free

VIBE CHECKS

“Vibe Check: GPT-6.2 Astra and Sol Leave Us Wanting More” https://every.?ev_audience=free by Katie Parrott https://every.?ev_audience=free/Vibe Check https://every.?ev_audience=free: OpenAI’s newest models are careful and candid: They follow the assignment, say when they fall short, and don’t game the test. But Astra drifts from the main point in longer drafts and reuses the same look in its designs (Kieran Klaassen https://every.?ev_audience=free of the frontier team https://every.?ev_audience=free kept getting mountains he never asked for). All six testers who rated Astra gave it yellow, and four of the five who rated Sol gave it red, so hand them clearly scoped work.

“Mini-Vibe Check: Four New Geminis. When Should You Pick Neon?” https://every.?ev_audience=free by Katie Parrott https://every.?ev_audience=free/Vibe Check https://every.?ev_audience=free: Google DeepMind added four models to its Gemini 4 lineup in little more than five weeks, and Neon, its newest, midweight model, is the one we’d pick for work we can steer. Katie rewrote her word processor so she could keep writing with Neon, and Kieran now pairs it with Opus 5.5 for coding at the keyboard. Mike says it made the best slide deck he’s seen from a Gemini model, but it burns through tokens.

“What We Let Our Agents Buy” https://every.?ev_audience=free by Grant Harvey https://every.?ev_audience=free/Context Window https://every.?ev_audience=free: ChatGPT Wallet makes it easier for agents to buy things, but the struggle to decide what to buy remains. ALIGNMENT

Ahhh. I’m lying on a carpeted floor around 4:30 p.m., my arms and legs spread out like a starfish. I’m breathing in, out, in, out, in a smooth rhythm. A tingling sensation spreads across my cheeks and darts through my hands and toes. Emotions start to bubble up in the center of my chest until anxiety arrives, tight and prickly. I welcome it like I’m saying hello to a dear old friend.

These are some of my notes from a breath work session on my second jhana retreat, run by Jhourney https://every.?ev_audience=free, which teaches techniques (or jhanas) for accessing the states of deep absorption and bliss described in Buddhist meditation. I returned to the retreat because I feel disconnected from myself. I’m preparing for a wedding, I’ve started a new job, and, for some masochistic reason, I’m building a biotech-focused media company. There’s been a lot of overwhelm and dissociation, making the past six months a blur.

I first heard of Jhourney through Dan’s podcast conversation https://every.?ev_audience=free with author and researcher Nadia Asparouhova. This time, the most valuable part was the relief of sitting with something difficult without giving myself a hard time for experiencing it. When anxiety came up, I imagined a guesthouse and invited it in. When I noticed myself resisting the anxiety, I welcomed that feeling, too. Giving both a place to be helped me feel more at home in myself.

I came back to London feeling grounded, and some of that is still with me. There’s still a wedding to plan and a company to build, but I want to practice being there for myself whenever life gets overwhelming. I’m working hard to build a life I want to live. I’d just like to be present for it.—Ashwin Sharma https://every.?ev_audience=free
